The story strikes an appropriate balance between scene and summary/exposition. It is anchored in a vivid, real-time scene—Marlen unlocking the door, stepping into the hallway, walking into the kitchen, and sitting by the window—which engages the reader through strong sensory details (the smell of dust and lavender, the creaking floorboards, the visual of the faded note). Instead of halting the narrative for lengthy blocks of exposition, the writer weaves necessary background information (her twenty-year absence, memories of her mother, her childhood habits) seamlessly into the real-time action as triggered by her surroundings. Finally, the story effectively uses summary at the very end ("Sie blieb sitzen, bis es dunkel wurde") to compress time and heighten the eerie tension for the concluding thought.
